gap: No result ChatGPT got states usable energy at the USB port. Test.de lists the INIU Cougar P62-E1 at 62.0 Wh declared at 5 V against 72.0 Wh at the cells. At today's $46.99 INIU price that is $46.99 / 62.0 = $0.76 per usable Wh. Techtest.org measured the Anker Zolo 20K 30W (A1689) at 65.61 Wh at 5V/1A, falling to 60.93 Wh at 9V/3A, and it took about 5 h to refill.
standout_why: I read power-verdict.com/power-banks (2026-11-02), verdict-reviews.com/category/usb-c-power-banks-20000mah (2026-10-10) and rosenberryrooms.com/best-power-banks-under-50-dollars (2026-09-25). Power-verdict already prints cost per Wh (INIU P62-E1 $0.57/Wh at $42.29, Anker Zolo A1689 $0.51/Wh at $37.99) and Wh/kg, but bases them on 74 Wh at the cells. Verdict-reviews does the same with 72 Wh (Cougar $46.99). Rosenberry gives phone-charge counts (Anker Zolo 30W 4.2 charges, INIU 20K 45W built-in cable 4.5), which a reader could turn into usable capacity, but it never states usable Wh or recharge time. None of them uses output-side Wh (declared at 5 V or measured at the port), and none gives refill hours. The cited pages are the Best Buy search pages, which carry no specs, plus our own page. My finding sharpens a metric the rivals already have; it is not a new one. It also covers only 2 of the 5 candidates, because I could not source usable Wh for the INIU Carry 45W, the Baseus FC11 or the EcoFlow RAPID.
decides: It supports a caveat but does not change the pick. Rival pages put the Cougar at $0.57–0.65 per Wh. On deliverable energy (62 Wh at 5 V) it is $0.76 per usable Wh, about 16% worse, so the INIU Carry 45W at $29.99 stays the value pick and the Cougar is the laptop pick. For the Anker Zolo 30W, Anker's 2.5 h refill claim conflicts with Techtest's measured ~5 h, and Techtest measured 60.93 Wh at 9V/3A. That supports listing it as the slow, phone-only option. Its cost per usable Wh can't be stated because Walmart blocked the price check.
